proposals.hypothesis: LiCaAlF6 is a Li-rich, wide-gap mixed fluoride. Its fluoride anion resists oxidation near 4 V. Ca2+ and Al3+ are hard to reduce and may compete with La for fluoride, so the La-containing products seen with LiF and Li3AlF6 (mainly LaF3 and LaPO4) could be less favored. This tests whether a second alkaline-earth cation changes the fluoride contact chemistry.
proposals.motivation: LiF and Li3AlF6 both gave the lowest penalties so far (about 0.099, bin 4), but still formed La-containing products, so a related fluoride with a different divalent cation is the next logical test.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electrically insulating Li-ion conductor that is thermodynamically stable toward Li7La3Zr2O12 (Li-rich, no reducible Zr/La exchange) and is an established coating for high-voltage cathodes. Its phosphate anion resists oxidation near 4 V, so it should limit Co-O/electrolyte interdiffusion and interfacial reaction with LLZO.

Li2ZrO3 is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide that shares Zr with LLZO, so Zr/Li exchange should not drive a reaction. Its oxide anion is far more compatible with the LLZO garnet than the phosphate in Li3PO4, which reacted with La and Zr to form LaPO4 and ZrO2. It should also resist oxidation near 4 V versus Li.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 gave a contact penalty of 0.099 eV/non-Li atom (bin 4) from LaPO4 and ZrO2 formation with LLZO, so a non-phosphate Li-rich oxide that avoids La-P reactivity is the next family to test.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3NbO4 is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide with Nb5+ in octahedral coordination. Its oxide anion should be more compatible with the LLZO garnet than the phosphate in Li3PO4, which formed LaPO4 and ZrO2. Nb5+ is hard to reduce, so it should resist reaction with Li-rich garnet and stay insulating near 4 V.
proposal.motivation: Li2ZrO3 (bin 4) and Li3PO4 (bin 14) both showed La-containing reaction products with LLZO. The lowest penalty so far came from a Li-rich oxide, so the next step is another Li-rich oxide with a different metal (Nb instead of Zr) to test whether the metal changes the interfacial reactivity.
